q-31382.name: Question 1
q-31382.problem: What is the coefficient of ${x}^{2}y$ in the product $(x-y)({x}^{2}+6xy-9{y}^{2})?$
q-31382.worked_solution:
We distribute all three terms of the binomial in the first set of parentheses to the trinomial in the second set of parentheses. Then, we simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-y)({x}^{2}+6xy-9{y}^{2}) & = \\ x({x}^{2}+6xy-9{y}^{2})+(-y)({x}^{2}+6xy-9{y}^{2}) & = \\ {x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}y-9x{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}y-6x{y}^{2}+9{y}^{3} & = \\ {x}^{3}+5{x}^{2}y-15x{y}^{2}+9{y}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coefficient of ${x}^{2}y$ is $5.$

q-31382.html:
Question 1
?

What is the coefficient of x2y in the product (x−y)(x2+6xy−9y2)?

a
7
b
−10
c
−15
d
−3
e
5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We distribute all three terms of the binomial in the first set of parentheses to the trinomial in the second set of parentheses. Then, we simplify:

(x−y)(x2+6xy−9y2)=x(x2+6xy−9y2)+(−y)(x2+6xy−9y2)=x3+6x2y−9xy2−x2y−6xy2+9y3=x3+5x2y−15xy2+9y3

Therefore, the coefficient of x2y is 5.

q-78170.name: Question 2
q-78170.worked_solution:
We distribute all three terms of the trinomial in the first set of parentheses to the trinomial in the second set of parentheses. Then, we simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}({p}^{2}+p+1)({p}^{2}+3p+1) & = \\ {p}^{2}({p}^{2}+3p+1)+p({p}^{2}+3p+1)+1({p}^{2}+3p+1) & = \\ {p}^{4}+3{p}^{3}+{p}^{2}+{p}^{3}+3{p}^{2}+p+{p}^{2}+3p+1 & = \\ {p}^{4}+4{p}^{3}+5{p}^{2}+4p+1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $a=4,$ $b=5,$ and $c=4.$ So, 

$$
a+b+c=4+5+4=13.
$$

q-78170.html:
Question 2
?

Given that (p2+p+1)(p2+3p+1)=p4+ap3+bp2+cp+1, calculate a+b+c.

a
13
b
8
c
18
d
15
e
11
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We distribute all three terms of the trinomial in the first set of parentheses to the trinomial in the second set of parentheses. Then, we simplify:

(p2+p+1)(p2+3p+1)=p2(p2+3p+1)+p(p2+3p+1)+1(p2+3p+1)=p4+3p3+p2+p3+3p2+p+p2+3p+1=p4+4p3+5p2+4p+1

Therefore, a=4, b=5, and c=4. So, a+b+c=4+5+4=13.

q-78171.name: Question 3
q-78171.worked_solution:
We distribute all three terms of the trinomial in the first set of parentheses to the trinomial in the second set of parentheses. Then, we simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}({t}^{2}+t+2)({t}^{2}+2t+1) & = \\ {t}^{2}({t}^{2}+2t+1)+t({t}^{2}+2t+1)+2({t}^{2}+2t+1) & = \\ {t}^{4}+2{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}+{t}^{3}+2{t}^{2}+t+2{t}^{2}+4t+2 & = \\ {t}^{4}+3{t}^{3}+5{t}^{2}+5t+2 & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $a=3,$ $b=5,$ and $c=5.$ So, 

$$
a+b+c=3+5+5=13.
$$

a
10
b
13
c
16
d
18
e
11
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We distribute all three terms of the trinomial in the first set of parentheses to the trinomial in the second set of parentheses. Then, we simplify:

(t2+t+2)(t2+2t+1)=t2(t2+2t+1)+t(t2+2t+1)+2(t2+2t+1)=t4+2t3+t2+t3+2t2+t+2t2+4t+2=t4+3t3+5t2+5t+2

Therefore, a=3, b=5, and c=5. So, a+b+c=3+5+5=13.
